climate.overview_html: August 29’s dominant climate story is escalation, not emergence. The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre triggered its Level 3 transboundary haze alert — its highest tier — on August 27 as smoke from Kalimantan and Sumatra put more than 5 million people on a respiratory emergency footing across Malaysia, Brunei, and Singapore, only the second activation of that threshold since the ASEAN haze-alert framework was established. The physical baseline sharpened this week: Copernicus C3S confirmed global sea surface temperatures reached 21.1°C on August 22 — the highest August ocean temperature ever recorded, striking because global SSTs should be declining from their March–April Southern Hemisphere peak, not setting new records. Against this, CTVC’s H1 2026 climate tech investment report documents a 55% funding surge to $26.1 billion, but 34% of it went to low-carbon data centers — the sector’s capital composition continues to diverge from deep-decarbonization priorities.

items.headline: ASEAN Level 3 Transboundary Haze Alert Triggered — Only Second Activation Ever; 5M+ People Exposed; Kalimantan and Sumatra Smoke Blankets Malaysia, Brunei, Singapore; Peak Season Warning
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) activated its highest-tier transboundary haze alert — Level 3 — on August 27, 2026 as widespread smoke from burning Kalimantan and Sumatra peatlands drove unhealthy air quality across Malaysia, Brunei, and Singapore. It is only the second Level 3 activation since the ASEAN framework was established, following the first in 2023. More than 5 million people across Borneo and Sumatra face direct respiratory risk; four zones in Malaysia have recorded “very unhealthy” API readings and Singapore is bracing for potential haze-crisis conditions. BNPB warns Indonesia is now entering the peak of its fire season (August–September), with El Niño-driven rainfall deficits forecast to persist through at least early September. Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry has formally called for collective ASEAN action under the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP). The SIIA Haze Outlook 2026, published in May, had pre-assigned a “Red” (highest) risk rating for August–September — only the second Red in the outlook’s history — based on the super El Niño and a concurrent positive Indian Ocean Dipole.

items.headline: Global Ocean Temperature Reaches 21.1°C on August 22 — Highest August SST Ever Recorded; Anomalous Because Oceans Typically Cool After Southern Hemisphere Summer; El Niño + Long-Term Forcing Converge
items.summary: Copernicus Climate Change Service confirmed that global mean sea surface temperature reached 21.1°C on August 22, 2026 — the highest value ever recorded for any August date in the satellite-era record. The finding is physically significant because global ocean temperatures normally decline from their March–April climatological peak, making a new all-time high in late August extraordinary. C3S attributes the record to the convergence of the developing super El Niño (Niño 3.4 already at +2.7°C) and the long-term anthropogenic ocean-warming trend that has raised mean SST by approximately 0.8°C since pre-industrial levels. The August record exceeds the previous all-time global ocean heat record of 21.09°C set in March 2024, itself already an outlier. Scientists warn the record-high August SST directly amplifies tropical cyclone intensification potential in all active basins, extends the fire-risk season in maritime Southeast Asia by maintaining anomalous atmospheric dryness, and accelerates coral bleaching across the Indo-Pacific.

items.headline: H1 2026 Climate Tech VC Surges 55% to $26.1 Billion — But Low-Carbon Data Centers Capture 34%; Deal Count Falls 25% as Capital Concentrates in Fewer Large Rounds; Adaptation Fastest-Growing Sub-Sector
items.summary: CTVC (formerly Sightline Climate) published its H1 2026 climate tech investment report, finding global climate technology venture and growth capital reached $26.1 billion in the first six months of 2026 — a 55% year-on-year increase and the strongest H1 for the sector since 2022. The headline growth conceals a structural shift: low-carbon data center technologies captured 34% of all H1 climate investment, up from just 3% a year earlier, driven by hyperscaler demand for clean-power computing. Data center developer DayOne raised $4.5 billion and Nscale raised $2 billion, together accounting for nearly two-thirds of all Series C climate funding in the half. Total deal count fell 25% year-on-year, confirming capital concentration in a smaller set of large, late-stage transactions. Climate adaptation funding grew 64% — the fastest-growing sub-sector by percentage. Nearly 28 cents of every climate equity dollar went to AI-enabled solutions. The pattern signals that climate tech VC in 2026 is being structurally reshaped by AI infrastructure demand rather than by decarbonization urgency.

items.headline: Malaysia’s National Carbon Market Policy Opens Carbon Credit Generation and Trading to Private Capital — Aligns With Paris Article 6; Peatland Preservation Economics Are Central Driver
items.summary: Malaysia’s National Carbon Market Policy (NCMP), which entered force April 21, 2026, opened its carbon credit generation, verification, and trading framework to private capital as of August 28, enabling private entities to generate verified credits from eligible mitigation projects across Malaysia’s forestry, peatland, and clean energy sectors. The timing is directly relevant to the ongoing Indonesia-Malaysia haze emergency: a functional domestic carbon market creates financial incentives for landowners to preserve peatlands rather than drain and burn them, addressing one of the root economic drivers of transboundary haze. The NCMP is designed for eventual alignment with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, allowing verified Malaysian credits to be used in other countries’ nationally determined contributions. Malaysia has simultaneously called for collective ASEAN action on transboundary haze, linking carbon market economics to the broader regional land-use governance challenge.

major_events.name: Typhoon Saudel — Weakening to Tropical Depression Post-Landfall; East China Flooding Ongoing; Wenzhou/Taizhou/Ningbo Inundated; Ports Progressively Reopening
major_events.status: WEAKENING TO TROPICAL DEPRESSION · FLOODING ONGOING · EAST CHINA PORTS REOPENING
major_events.impact: After its double landfall on the Zhejiang coast on August 28 (Yuhuan 8:05 AM CST at 35 m/s, Wenzhou 9:10 AM CST at 33 m/s), Typhoon Saudel is weakening rapidly toward tropical depression strength on August 29 as it tracks westward. Post-landfall winds eased to approximately 108 km/h and are forecast to fall to tropical depression thresholds by August 29–30. East China ports disrupted on August 28 — including 197 grounded flights and Shanghai supply-chain impacts — are progressively reopening as winds ease. However, the rainfall threat remains acute: locally more than 500 mm has fallen in parts of Zhejiang, falling on soils already saturated by Typhoon Narra three days earlier. Flash flooding and mudslides are ongoing across Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Ningbo lowlands. Saudel is the third typhoon to strike Zhejiang in 2026, an unusually concentrated sequence that has progressively saturated the region’s drainage basins.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Dolly — Formed August 28, Dissipated August 29 as Open Tropical Wave; Fourth Named Storm of 2026 Atlantic Season; Leeward Islands Heavy-Rain Threat This Weekend
major_events.status: DISSIPATED · OPEN TROPICAL WAVE · LEEWARD ISLANDS RAIN THREAT SAT–SUN
major_events.impact: Tropical Storm Dolly formed on August 28 from the near-Bermuda area that carried 40% development odds in yesterday’s digest, becoming the fourth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic season. NHC initiated advisories at 11 AM EST with Dolly at 1,555 miles east of the Leeward Islands, tracking west at 24 mph with 40 mph sustained winds. By August 29, NHC discontinued advisories after observing the loss of a closed circulation; the system downgraded to an open tropical wave in under 24 hours as El Niño wind shear re-asserted itself. The remnant moisture signature is forecast to approach the Lesser Antilles Saturday night into Sunday, with heavy rainfall and flash-flood potential in higher terrain. The rapid lifecycle — named storm to dissipated wave in under 24 hours — is consistent with NOAA’s below-normal 2026 Atlantic season forecast.

major_events.name: US Southwest/South Heat Dome — Still Active August 29; 98 Million at Heat Risk; Phoenix 107–118°F; Extreme Heat Warnings Through 8 PM; No Pattern Break Until Early September
major_events.status: ONGOING · 98M AFFECTED · PHOENIX 107–118°F · WARNINGS THROUGH 8 PM AUG 29
major_events.impact: The US Southwest and South heat dome remains active August 29 with approximately 98 million people facing major or extreme heat risk across the region. NWS extreme heat warnings extend through 8 PM Saturday across the Phoenix metro area (107–115°F afternoon highs), southwest Arizona, and southeast California (106–118°F). Overnight lows in the 85–90°F range across much of the affected region continue to prevent physiological recovery. AccuWeather and NWS medium-range guidance show the sustaining ridge beginning to weaken but meaningful relief will not reach Texas and the southern Plains until early September. Dallas stands at 27 days at or above 100°F in August 2026. Cooling centers in Phoenix, Dallas, and Houston are operating at or beyond designed capacity.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — Upgraded to HELD Status August 27; 6 Orders and 3 Alerts; 25,000 ha Burned; 150 Structures Damaged; Phased Return Process May Begin
major_events.impact: BC Wildfire Service upgraded the Bald Range wildfire near Summerland to “held” status on August 27 at approximately 7 PM, meaning the fire is projected to remain within its current perimeter given existing suppression resources and forecast weather — a meaningful improvement from the active mop-up phase of yesterday’s digest. Six evacuation orders and three evacuation alerts remain active (down from ten alerts at peak); residents of the highest-risk zones still cannot return. The fire has burned approximately 25,000 hectares since its August 7 ignition and damaged or destroyed roughly 150 structures. One fatality was confirmed on August 27 when an 80-year-old woman died evacuating from Meadow Valley. BC Wildfire Service indicated a phased re-entry process for lower-risk zones may begin pending fire-behavior assessment over the coming days.

major_events.name: Indonesia/Southeast Asia Wildfire & Haze — ASEAN Level 3 Alert; 5M+ Exposed; 30 Aircraft Deployed; Malaysia Schools Still Closed; Peak Fire Season Warning Through September
major_events.status: ASEAN LEVEL 3 · 5M+ EXPOSED · 30 AIRCRAFT · PEAK SEASON AUG–SEP
major_events.impact: Indonesia’s wildfire and haze emergency escalated to ASEAN Level 3 on August 27 as smoke from Kalimantan and Sumatra put more than 5 million people on respiratory emergency footing. BNPB’s 30-aircraft suppression and cloud-seeding fleet remains deployed, with cross-border operations coordinated in Malaysian Sarawak airspace. Some 13,500 people have been treated for respiratory infections since July. Malaysia’s schools in affected Sarawak districts remain closed; outdoor National Day events on August 31 are under threat. BNPB warns Indonesia is entering peak fire season with El Niño-driven rainfall deficits expected to persist through at least early September, maintaining extreme peatland-fire conditions.

major_events.name: Europe Wildfire/Drought Emergency — 626,818 ha EU-Wide; Danube Critically Low; Paks Nuclear Output Curtailed; Blocking Pattern Locked
major_events.status: ONGOING · 626,818 HA · DANUBE CRITICALLY LOW · PAKS OUTPUT REDUCED
major_events.impact: Europe’s combined wildfire and drought emergency continues without material change from yesterday’s assessment. JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area at 626,818 hectares from 1,797 fires, tracking 33% ahead of the same date in the record 2025 season. Very-extreme fire danger indices persist across the Romania–Hungary corridor; extreme danger extends to southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. The Danube is at critically low stage and Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues to curtail output because cooling-water discharge temperatures exceed permitted environmental limits. The atmospheric blocking pattern sustaining the Eastern European heat anomaly shows no credible medium-range breakdown signal.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — 107+ Dead Since June; Flash Flood Risk Continuing Across Punjab, KP, Sindh
major_events.status: ONGOING · 107+ DEAD · FLASH FLOODING · PUNJAB / KP / SINDH
major_events.impact: Pakistan’s cumulative monsoon death toll stands at 107 or above per PDMA reporting since June. PMD continues issuing flash-flood and heavy-rain advisories for successive pulse events across Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Sindh. While PMD’s seasonal forecast calls for slightly below-normal aggregate rainfall nationally, short-duration intense precipitation events are producing localized flash flooding that existing drainage infrastructure cannot absorb. The monsoon season is climatologically active through September; further heavy-rain pulses are forecast in the coming week.

Tropical Storm Dolly — which formed August 28 from the near-Bermuda area at yesterday’s 40% odds — dissipated within 24 hours as an open tropical wave as El Niño shear re-asserted; NHC discontinued advisories after observing no closed circulation, though the remnant moisture threatens heavy rain across the Leeward Islands this weekend. Meanwhile, Typhoon Saudel is weakening to tropical depression strength post-landfall as East China ports progressively reopen, though flash flooding from locally 500+ mm rainfall continues across Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Ningbo. items.headline: Tropical Storm Dolly Forms August 28, Dissipates Within 24 Hours; Fourth Named Storm of 2026 Atlantic Season; El Niño Shear Ends Brief Window; Leeward Islands Heavy Rain Threat Remains
items.summary: Tropical Storm Dolly formed August 28 from the near-Bermuda disturbance that carried 40% development odds in NHC’s August 27 outlooks, becoming the fourth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic season. At 11 AM EST Dolly was 1,555 miles east of the Leeward Islands, tracking west at 24 mph with 40 mph sustained winds. By August 29, NHC discontinued advisories after observations showed the loss of a closed circulation — the system degraded to an open tropical wave in under 24 hours as the favorable shear window closed and El Niño-driven wind shear reasserted itself over the MDR. Despite dissipation, the remnant moisture will approach the Lesser Antilles Saturday night into Sunday, with heavy rainfall and flash-flood potential in higher terrain. The rapid lifecycle is consistent with NOAA’s below-normal 2026 Atlantic season forecast attributing suppression to El Niño shear.

items.headline: Typhoon Saudel Weakens Toward Tropical Depression Post-Double-Landfall; East China Ports Reopening; Flooding Persists Across Wenzhou–Taizhou–Ningbo With Locally 500+ mm Rainfall on Saturated Soils
items.summary: Typhoon Saudel, which made double landfall on Zhejiang’s coast August 28 (Yuhuan at 8:05 AM CST at 35 m/s, Wenzhou at 9:10 AM CST at 33 m/s), is weakening rapidly post-landfall and is forecast to reach tropical depression intensity by August 29–30 as it tracks westward. Post-landfall winds eased to approximately 108 km/h and are falling. However, the accumulated rainfall threat remains the dominant concern: locally more than 500 mm fell in parts of Zhejiang on soils already at field capacity from Typhoon Narra three days earlier, producing ongoing flash flooding and mudslides across the Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Ningbo lowlands. items.headline: US Heat Dome Still Active August 29: 98 Million at Risk; Phoenix Metro 107–118°F; Extreme Heat Warnings Through 8 PM; Overnight Lows 85–90°F Prevent Recovery; No Break Until Early September
items.summary: The US Southwest and South heat dome remains active August 29 with NWS extreme heat warnings through 8 PM across the Phoenix metro area (107–115°F), southwest Arizona, and southeast California (106–118°F). Approximately 98 million people from the Southwest to the southern Plains and Texas face major or extreme heat risk through the end of August. The overnight low temperature regime — 85–90°F across much of the region — continues to prevent physiological recovery, representing the greatest risk to heat-vulnerable populations without air conditioning. AccuWeather and NWS ensemble guidance show the sustaining upper-level ridge beginning to weaken but meaningful temperature relief will not reach Texas and the southern Plains until early September. renewables.overview_html: The IEA’s Global Energy Review 2026 delivers a structural milestone: global renewable capacity additions hit a record 800 GW in 2025, with solar PV alone accounting for ~600 GW and posting a +600 TWh generation increase the IEA describes as the largest single-year output gain ever recorded for any energy source in history — the first time a modern renewable source delivered the largest share of global energy demand growth. On the infrastructure side, Pattern Energy’s SunZia Wind project in eastern New Mexico confirmed commercial operations in June 2026 — at 3,650 MW the largest wind development in the Western Hemisphere, with 916 turbines and a 550-mile transmission corridor to Arizona and Southern California. India confirmed a record 29 GW of combined solar and wind addition in H1 2026, keeping the country on track for its 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030.

items.headline: IEA Global Energy Review 2026: Solar PV Posts +600 TWh — Largest Single-Year Generation Gain in History for Any Energy Source; 800 GW Global Renewables Capacity Record; Solar First to Lead Global Demand Growth
items.summary: The IEA’s Global Energy Review 2026 confirms that 2025 set the most significant renewable energy deployment record since the clean energy era began. Global annual renewable capacity additions reached 800 GW — a new record — with solar PV accounting for approximately 600 GW (75%) of total additions. Most significantly, solar PV’s absolute generation increase of +600 TWh in 2025 is the largest single-year generation gain ever recorded for any energy source in the IEA’s datasets, surpassing peak coal and natural gas growth years. Solar PV’s global generation reached nearly 2,700 TWh — more than double its 2022 output — with share of global electricity exceeding 8%. For the first time on record, a modern renewable source (solar) met more than 25% of the world’s additional energy demand growth. China commissioned nearly 370 GW of solar in 2025; the EU added a record 85 GW of renewable capacity with Spain achieving a record 14 GW solar addition. The IEA notes that global renewables expansion reached its 23rd consecutive record year in 2025.

items.source: EIA Today in Energy / Pattern Energy
items.headline: Pattern Energy’s SunZia Wind Project Commissioned at 3,650 MW — Largest Wind Development in the Western Hemisphere; 916 Turbines; 550-Mile Transmission to Arizona and Southern California
items.summary: The US Energy Information Administration confirmed commercial operations for Pattern Energy’s SunZia Wind project in eastern New Mexico, the largest wind development ever built in the Western Hemisphere at 3,650 MW net summer capacity. The $11 billion project — nearly two decades from initial planning to completion — comprises 916 wind turbines across the Estancia Valley, paired with a 550-mile direct-current transmission corridor delivering power to Arizona and Southern California. SunZia’s capacity is more than three times that of the next-largest US wind projects (Alta Wind at 1,098 MW and Great Prairie at 1,027 MW). The project reached initial testing operations in April 2026, with full commercial operations confirmed in June 2026. At full capacity SunZia will deliver clean power equivalent to approximately 3 million US homes, representing a step-change in the scale of individual renewable energy projects that US market economics can support.

science.overview_html: August’s most consequential result for operational AI weather forecasting: a paper published in Science Advances and covered by Carbon Brief establishes that ECMWF’s HRES systematically outperforms GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, and FuXi specifically for record-breaking extremes: AI models consistently underestimate both the frequency and magnitude of record-breaking heat, cold, and wind events, with errors growing as the degree of record exceedance increases — meaning AI is most deficient precisely when accurate forecasting matters most. On the applied side, ECMWF announced August 27 the operational deployment of AIFL, an LSTM-based global streamflow model trained on 18,588 river basins that detected a 20-year flood signal six days before Storm Henk’s January 2024 Belgium floods. A parallel GRL paper and AIES journal study extend the AI-vs-NWP evaluation to atmospheric rivers and severe convective environments respectively, building a consistent picture: AI weather models excel on average-skill metrics but underperform physics-based systems for the coherent, high-impact weather structures that drive the largest societal losses.

items.headline: Science Advances: Physics-Based HRES Outperforms GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, and FuXi for Record-Breaking Extremes — AI Models Underestimate Frequency and Magnitude; Errors Grow With Record Exceedance
items.meta: UNIGE & collaborators · Science Advances · DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aec1433 · preprint arXiv:2508.15724
items.summary: A study published in Science Advances provides the first systematic comparison of ECMWF HRES against three leading AI weather prediction models — GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, and FuXi — specifically for record-breaking extreme events. The headline finding: HRES consistently outperforms all three AI models for record-breaking heat, cold, and wind events across nearly all forecast lead times. AI model forecast errors are larger for record-breaking extremes than for standard conditions, and the errors grow as the magnitude of record exceedance increases — AI is most deficient when it matters most operationally. AI models tend to underpredict hot records and overestimate cold records. The University of Geneva-led team cautions that benchmarks based on average skill over all weather conditions — the dominant evaluation paradigm that drove claims of AI superiority — systematically mask tail-distribution deficiencies. The finding lands directly in the operational context of WeatherNext Cyclones’ debut last week and is reshaping validation frameworks for next-generation AI weather systems including AIFS. Carbon Brief’s coverage brought the result to wide community attention; UNIGE issued a press release stating “AI falls short in predicting weather extremes.”

items.headline: ECMWF Operationally Deploys AIFL: Deterministic LSTM Global Streamflow Model Trained on 18,588 Basins; Detects 20-Year Flood Signal 6 Days in Advance; Enters Copernicus EMS Flood Service
items.summary: ECMWF announced the operational deployment of AIFL (AI for Floods) on August 27, 2026 within the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) global flood forecasting component. AIFL is a deterministic long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network designed for global daily streamflow forecasting, trained on 18,588 river basins from the CARAVAN dataset using a two-stage approach: pre-training on 40 years of ERA5-Land reanalysis to learn robust basin dynamics, then fine-tuned on IFS control forecasts to adapt to operational forecast biases. Independent test performance (2021–2024): median modified Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE′) of 0.66 and median Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of 0.53 globally across all 18,588 basins. Most operationally significant: AIFL detected a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance during the January 2024 Storm Henk floods in Belgium — a lead time large enough to support meaningful evacuation and infrastructure-protection decisions. The deployment marks the first ML streamflow model to enter operational service within the Copernicus Emergency Management System.

items.headline: GRL: HRES Outperforms Five ML Models in Atmospheric River Detection Skill for Days 1–4; PanguWeather Matches HRES Beyond Day 4 — First Systematic AR Evaluation of AI Weather Models on US West Coast
items.meta: Davis et al. · Geophysical Research Letters · DOI: 10.1029/2025GL117609
items.summary: A study in Geophysical Research Letters presents the first systematic evaluation of five AI weather models — Aurora, GraphCast, PanguWeather, FourCastNetV2, and FourCastNet — specifically for atmospheric river (AR) forecasting affecting the US West Coast, where ARs drive the majority of extreme precipitation and flood events. The headline result: ECMWF HRES shows superior AR detection skill for the first four forecast days across all five ML models; PanguWeather is the only ML model to match HRES AR detection skill beyond day four. While ML models often achieve better variable-specific RMSE on standard benchmarks (notably 500 hPa geopotential height), their ability to correctly detect the coherent spatial structure of a narrow, high-moisture AR corridor lags HRES in the critical short-to-medium range. The result directly complements the Science Advances extremes paper: a consistent pattern emerges in which AI models excel on aggregate average-skill metrics but underperform physics-based models for the coherent, structured, high-impact weather systems — atmospheric rivers, record extremes, and tropical cyclones — that drive the largest societal losses.

items.source: AMS / Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
items.headline: AIES: Severe Weather Forecasts From AI Weather Prediction Models — Random Forest Downscaling of PanguWeather, FourcastNet v2, GraphCast Achieves Skillful Severe Weather Prediction at 7–8 Day Lead Times
items.meta: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems · Vol. 5, Issue 1 · 2026
items.summary: Published in the AMS journal Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems, this paper evaluates three leading AI weather prediction models — PanguWeather, FourcastNet v2-small, and GraphCast — as environments for severe weather prediction at 1–8 day lead times, using random forest models trained on surface observations to downscale AI-NWP output. The study finds AI-based weather prediction model environments can support skillful severe weather prediction at 7–8 day leads that historically matched NWP skill at only 3–5 day leads, representing a meaningful extension of effective severe weather predictability. However, skill gains are strongest for bulk thermodynamic and kinematic environment metrics (CAPE, shear, hodograph shape) rather than for specific hazard types like tornado or hail, consistent with the broader pattern: AI models perform better for large-scale atmospheric state variables than for spatially discrete convective initiation or hazard occurrence. The paper provides the first systematic multi-model AIWP severe weather skill assessment in a peer-reviewed AMS journal.

items.headline: arXiv 2606.21170: Weighted Potential CRPS Enables Fair Comparisons of AI and Physics-Based Weather Models for Extreme Events — Standard Metrics Systematically Underweight Tail Performance
items.summary: This preprint proposes the Weighted Potential Continuous Ranked Probability Score (WPCRPS) as a correction to the evaluation bias that has allowed AI weather models to claim superiority over physics-based NWP on standard metrics while potentially underperforming on high-impact extreme events. Standard CRPS and RMSE score metrics weight all forecast errors equally regardless of whether they involve extreme or moderate conditions — a design choice that systematically discounts performance at the tails of the distribution where operational forecasting failures cause the greatest societal harm. The WPCRPS applies user-defined threshold weights to the scoring function, enabling model comparisons that reflect the asymmetric value of accurate extreme-event forecasting. Applied to leading AI weather models and ECMWF HRES on a common benchmark, the paper shows that the apparent skill advantage of AI models narrows or reverses under WPCRPS when the weighting emphasizes the extreme tail. The methodological contribution directly addresses the evaluation framework gap highlighted by the Science Advances extreme-event outperformance paper published earlier in 2026, and is being considered for adoption in community NWP intercomparison protocols.

items.headline: arXiv 2606.25076: Machine Learning Is Revolutionizing Weather Forecasting — The Next Step Is a Change in How We Work; Systematic Assessment of Operational Integration Challenges for AI-NWP
items.summary: This perspective paper on arXiv from a group of operational meteorologists and AI researchers argues that while data-driven ML weather models have demonstrably transformed medium-range forecast skill, the next bottleneck is organizational and operational rather than technical: how do operational centers integrate AI-NWP into forecast workflows, quality-control chains, and uncertainty-quantification frameworks designed for physics-based models? The paper identifies five structural gaps: (1) ML models lack physically interpretable uncertainty estimates native to ensemble NWP; (2) ML model failure modes for novel conditions (record extremes, climate-shifted basins) are poorly characterized in operational settings; (3) post-processing and statistical calibration pipelines built for NWP output do not transfer directly to AI-NWP; (4) operational data assimilation cycles that feed NWP initialization are not yet designed to exploit ML model speed; and (5) ML model training pipelines require governance frameworks for version control and reproducibility comparable to those developed for operational NWP software. The paper is positioned as a practitioner-facing complement to the wave of technical AI-NWP publications and is receiving broad engagement from NWP centers including ECMWF, NOAA, and national Met services.

items.title: MSCI Acquires Climate Risk Data Provider First Street for $120 Million — Embeds Parcel-Level Physical Hazard Into Financial Risk Infrastructure; Deal Expected to Close Q3 2026
items.body_html: MSCI announced on June 26, 2026 the acquisition of First Street, the US-based physical climate risk modeling company, for $120 million in cash at close with contingent earnout payments tied to revenue thresholds in the first two years post-close. The deal is expected to close in Q3 2026, making it an imminent completion at the time of this digest. First Street has built the most widely cited consumer-facing physical climate risk dataset in the US, covering flood, fire, heat, and wind risk at the individual parcel level for every US property; its data underpin major real estate platforms, municipal planning frameworks, and regulatory climate-disclosure initiatives. For MSCI, the acquisition directly embeds property-level physical climate hazard into the firm’s global financial risk infrastructure — the same platform used by institutional investors for equity factor exposure, credit risk, and ESG scoring. The deal accelerates the convergence of physical climate risk modeling and financial market infrastructure that regulators including the SEC, Bank of England, and ECB are mandating through climate-related financial disclosure requirements. Fintech Global noted First Street’s hyperlocal hazard data is a key differentiator that MSCI could not replicate through organic development at comparable resolution.

items.body_html: Malaysia’s National Carbon Market Policy (NCMP), which entered force April 21, 2026, opened its carbon credit generation, verification, and trading framework to private capital as of August 28, enabling private entities to generate verified credits from eligible mitigation projects across Malaysia’s forestry, peatland, and clean energy sectors. The timing is directly relevant to the ongoing Indonesia-Malaysia haze emergency: a functional domestic carbon market creates financial incentives for landowners to preserve peatlands rather than drain and burn them, addressing one of the root economic drivers of transboundary haze. The NCMP is structured for eventual alignment with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement’s international carbon market mechanisms, which would allow verified Malaysian credits to be used by other countries toward their nationally determined contributions. Malaysia has simultaneously called for collective ASEAN action on haze, with the Foreign Ministry linking carbon market economics to the broader regional land-use governance challenge facing Borneo and Sumatra peatlands.
